scenarios.title: M0 · Normal Sinus
scenarios.description: Maintain VVI standby pacing while observing intrinsic beats.
scenarios.objective: Confirm the pacemaker remains inhibited while the patient maintains an intrinsic sinus rate.
scenarios.feedback: No pacing spikes should be visible. If pacing occurs, lower the rate below the intrinsic rhythm or verify sensing leads.

scenarios.title: M1 · Symptomatic Bradycardia
scenarios.description: Patient with symptomatic ventricular bradycardia requiring VVI demand pacing.
scenarios.objective: Increase the VVI pacing rate above the intrinsic 34–38 ppm rhythm with adequate output and sensitivity to achieve consistent ventricular capture.
scenarios.feedback: Start VVI pacing, set the rate to 60–70 ppm, output to 5–10 mA, and sensitivity around 2 mV to obtain paced QRS complexes.

rules.description: Loss of capture when pacing output is inadequate despite the higher rate.

effects.feedback: Raise the output to at least 5 mA and reassess capture at the paced rate.

rules.description: Oversensing inhibits pacing when sensitivity is set too low (too sensitive).

effects.feedback: Reduce sensitivity toward ~2 mV so that only true R-waves are sensed and pacing is not inappropriately inhibited.

rules.description: Stable ventricular capture once rate, output, and sensitivity are set appropriately.

effects.feedback: Paced rhythm should be stable at the selected rate with each pacing spike followed by a QRS complex.

scenarios.title: M2 · Capture Threshold Test
scenarios.description: Determine the ventricular capture threshold and program an appropriate safety margin.

alarm.text: Begin threshold test – rate above intrinsic

scenarios.objective: Increase the VVI rate above the intrinsic rhythm, slowly reduce the output to find the minimal output that consistently captures, then program a final output with a 2–3× safety margin.
scenarios.feedback: Set the rate to ≥70 ppm, decrease output until capture is lost, then increase until every spike captures. Set final output about 2–3× higher.

rules.description: During the threshold search, output is too low and capture is lost.

alarm.text: Loss of capture – slowly increase output

effects.feedback: You are below the capture threshold. Increase the output in small steps until each pacing spike is followed by a QRS complex.

rules.description: Output is set at the threshold with no safety margin.

alarm.text: Output at threshold – add safety margin

effects.feedback: You have found the capture threshold, but the output should be increased to about 2–3× this value to ensure long-term capture.

rules.description: Stable capture with appropriate safety margin programmed.

alarm.text: Stable capture – threshold and margin set

effects.feedback: All beats are paced at the programmed rate and each spike results in a QRS complex. The programmed output provides an adequate safety margin above the threshold.

scenarios.title: M3 · Sensing & Undersensing
scenarios.description: Determine the ventricular sensing threshold and correct undersensing.
scenarios.primaryRhythm: Intrinsic sinus rhythm with intermittent pacing

alarm.text: Set rate below intrinsic and minimize output

scenarios.objective: With the rate set below the intrinsic rhythm and output minimized, adjust Sensitivity to find the sensing threshold, recognize undersensing, and program a safe sensitivity setting.
scenarios.feedback: Set rate at 40–60 ppm and output very low (0–2 mA). Decrease mV (more sensitive) until intrinsic R-waves are reliably sensed and pacing is inhibited.

rules.description: Undersensing: pacemaker paces despite intrinsic QRS because sensitivity (mV) is too high (too insensitive).

effects.feedback: Pacing spikes occur despite intrinsic QRS complexes. Lower the mV setting until R-waves are detected reliably and pacing is inhibited appropriately.

rules.description: Intrinsic rhythm is reliably sensed and pacing is appropriately inhibited.

effects.feedback: SENSE corresponds to intrinsic QRS complexes and pacing is inhibited whenever intrinsic beats occur.

scenarios.title: M4 · Oversensing & Inhibition
scenarios.description: Recognize oversensing that leads to inappropriate inhibition of pacing and correct it.

alarm.text: Oversensing – long pauses due to pacing inhibition

scenarios.objective: Identify oversensing that inhibits pacing and correct it by decreasing sensitivity (raising mV) without causing undersensing.
scenarios.feedback: When mV is too low (too sensitive), sensing responds to noise/T-waves and pacing is inhibited. Raise mV until oversensing disappears while true QRS complexes are still sensed.

rules.description: Oversensing due to very high sensitivity (low mV) leading to pauses.

effects.feedback: SENSE flashes occur without true QRS complexes and pacing is inhibited, producing long pauses. Increase the mV setting until oversensing disappears.

rules.description: Oversensing corrected; pacing supports the patient appropriately.

effects.feedback: SENSE corresponds to real QRS complexes only, and pacing occurs when intrinsic beats are absent.

scenarios.title: M5 · Threshold Drift & Loss of Capture
scenarios.description: Recognize evolving loss of capture and readjust output after threshold drift.
scenarios.summaryLabel: Threshold drift and loss of capture
scenarios.primaryRhythm: Ventricular pacing with evolving loss of capture

alarm.text: Intermittent loss of capture – reassess threshold

scenarios.objective: Identify intermittent loss of capture and increase output to restore stable capture with a safety margin.
scenarios.feedback: Repeat a capture threshold check and increase output until every pacing spike captures again, then maintain a 2–3× safety margin.

rules.description: Output is below threshold leading to complete loss of capture.

alarm.text: Complete loss of capture – increase output

effects.feedback: No QRS complexes follow pacing spikes. Increase the output and reassess threshold.

rules.description: Output near threshold causing intermittent loss of capture.

effects.feedback: Some spikes capture while others do not. Increase output to restore a safety margin.

rules.description: Output increased; capture restored with safety margin.

effects.feedback: All spikes now result in QRS complexes again. Monitor for further threshold changes.

scenarios.title: M6 · PVCs & PACs in VVI
scenarios.description: Recognize ectopic beats on the ECG during VVI pacing and understand their interaction with pacemaker timing.
scenarios.objective: Identify ectopic beats and explain how sensed beats reset or inhibit pacing without mistaking ectopy for device malfunction.
scenarios.feedback: With appropriate VVI settings, you should see paced beats interrupted by occasional ectopy. Recognize morphology/timing and avoid unnecessary parameter changes.

rules.description: Pacemaker appropriately programmed; ectopy present but device function is normal.

effects.feedback: Occasional ectopy occurs while pacing behaviour remains appropriate. No parameter changes are required.

scenarios.title: M7 · Wide vs Narrow QRS
scenarios.description: Differentiate intrinsic narrow QRS complexes from wide QRS paced beats and ectopic beats.
scenarios.objective: Distinguish intrinsic narrow QRS from wide paced beats and ectopy, and understand that wide QRS is expected in ventricular pacing.
scenarios.feedback: Identify intrinsic beats vs paced beats (spike + wide QRS) vs ectopy (premature wide beat without spike).

rules.description: Parameters acceptable; scenario focuses on ECG interpretation.

effects.feedback: Focus on distinguishing intrinsic narrow QRS, paced wide QRS, and ectopy based on morphology and the presence/absence of pacing spikes.

scenarios.title: C1 · Third-degree AV Block
scenarios.description: Complete AV dissociation with a slow ventricular escape rhythm.

alarm.text: Complete heart block – stabilise the patient

scenarios.objective: Stabilise a patient with complete heart block by establishing reliable ventricular pacing.
scenarios.feedback: Initiate VVI pacing with adequate rate and output. Confirm capture (spike followed by QRS) and appropriate sensing.

scenarios.title: C2 · Second-degree AV Block (Mobitz II)
scenarios.description: Intermittent non-conducted P waves with dropped QRS complexes (placeholder rhythm using no-conduction template).
scenarios.objective: Recognise dropped ventricular beats and be prepared to provide pacing support if perfusion worsens.
scenarios.feedback: Identify conducted vs non-conducted P waves. If pauses are symptomatic, increase VVI rate and ensure adequate output and sensing.

scenarios.title: C3 · Sick Sinus Syndrome
scenarios.description: Sinus node dysfunction with inappropriate bradycardia and pauses (placeholder using brady escape rhythm).
scenarios.objective: Recognise sinus pauses and decide when pacing support is needed to maintain perfusion.
scenarios.feedback: If symptomatic or prolonged pauses occur, enable pacing and set rate above the escape rhythm. Confirm capture and appropriate inhibition.

scenarios.title: C4 · Slow Conduction
scenarios.description: Markedly delayed conduction with a slow ventricular response (uses slow-conduction waveform).
scenarios.primaryRhythm: Marked first-degree block / slow ventricular conduction
scenarios.objective: Identify slow conduction and support ventricular rate with pacing if clinically indicated.
scenarios.feedback: If perfusion is inadequate, enable pacing and set a safe lower rate limit. Ensure sensing is appropriate and pacing is not inhibited incorrectly.
